result.markdown:
For a small company, I'd recommend choosing an HR system that's **easy to use, affordable, and capable of growing with the business** without needing a dedicated HR manager to run it.

If you're a UK-based small business, there are several excellent options. My shortlist would be\:

## Best HR software options

(Best overall for small UK businesses)

Indicative pricing: from £24/month

- Employee records and document storage
- Holiday and sickness tracking
- Onboarding and performance reviews
- Simple, UK-focused HR administration

Best if you want straightforward HR without unnecessary complexity.

[Visit Breathe HR](https://www.breathehr.com/)

Good for companies without an internal HR department.

## My recommendation

For most small UK businesses, I'd narrow it down as follows\:

| Your requirement | My choice |
|--------|--------|
| Simple, affordable HR | Breathe HR |
| Startup with a small team | CharlieHR |
| Employment law advice | BrightHR |
| HR and payroll together | Employment Hero |
| Growing business with more complex needs | Factorial |


**I'd start by looking at Breathe HR and CharlieHR.** They are good starting points if you mainly need employee records, holiday requests, sickness tracking, contracts and onboarding.

## A few questions to find the best fit

The right recommendation depends quite a lot on your company.

1. **How many employees do you have?**
2. **Do you need payroll included, or just HR management?**
3. **What industry are you in?** For example, construction, hospitality, retail, professional services or manufacturing.

With those three details, I can narrow it down to the best two or three systems and compare their costs, features and suitability for your business.

search_results.description: TechRadar’s 2026 guide evaluates leading HR software for payroll, compliance, recruitment, onboarding, benefits, performance management, and employee administration. Gusto is named best overall for its full-service payroll, time tracking, benefits administration, compliance support, and HR guidance. Employment Hero is recommended for small and medium-sized businesses because of its customizable workflows, automation, AI assistant, and broad feature set, though advanced functions and add-ons can increase costs. Rippling is best for versatility, particularly for distributed teams, offering remote device management, tax registration, scalable services, and per-employee billing. Other recommendations include Remote Payroll for international enterprises, BambooHR as an all-in-one system, Zoho People for integrations, Breathe HR for simple employee management, Deel for powerful global HR capabilities, PeopleHR for mobile access, Paylocity for mid-sized businesses, Staffology Payroll for complex enterprise payroll, Workable for recruitment, and BrightHR for extensive workforce-management features. The guide advises selecting software according to company size and specific workflow needs, and explains that testing considered usability, features, security, support, pricing, and user feedback.
